section_summary: This section contains State Department records from 1945 to 1949 regarding the postwar status, trusteeship, and occupation of Pacific islands and Japan. The early documents comprise internal memoranda and public petitions concerning whether the former Japanese mandated islands, the Bonins, and the Volcano Islands should be placed under United Nations trusteeship or retained as United States military bases. Subsequent materials document Far Eastern Commission debates on Japanese occupation costs and reparations, strategies to prevent Soviet or Chinese expansion of occupation forces in Japan, and a comprehensive 1949 report detailing difficult economic, administrative, and social conditions in occupied Okinawa.

subfiles.about: Discusses the proposed disposition of Marcus, Bonin, Volcano, and Japanese Mandated islands under trusteeship or base arrangements.
subfiles.summary: Analyzes whether Marcus, Bonin, Volcano, and Mandated islands should be placed under trusteeship or annexed as United States military bases.
subfiles.title: Some Thoughts On Marcus Island, Bonin Islands, Volcano Islands, and the Japanese Mandated Islands

subfiles.about: Reminds Stewart to consult Ben Gerig regarding trusteeship formulas and discusses leasing Pacific islands for defense.
subfiles.summary: Reminds Stewart to consult Ben Gerig on trusteeship formulas and endorses General Embick's proposal to lease strategic Pacific islands.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Trusteeship Formula and Pacific Island Leases

subfiles.about: Transmits a research study on missionary influence on Pacific colonial policy in response to Consul Sokobin's inquiries.
subfiles.summary: Transmits a research study on nineteenth-century missionary influence on colonial policy in the Pacific to Consul Sokobin in Birmingham.
subfiles.title: Instruction Transmitting Study on Missionary Influence in the Pacific
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in charge, Birmingham

subfiles.about: Refers an incoming communication concerning the Japanese Mandated Islands to the Department of State.
subfiles.summary: Executive Clerk M. C. Latta refers an incoming communication regarding the Japanese Mandated Islands to the Department of State.
subfiles.title: White House Referral Slip

subfiles.about: Urges the President to place the Japanese Mandated Islands under United Nations trusteeship with civilian rather than naval administration.
subfiles.from: John Collier, Richard Wood, Owen J. Roberts, Norman Thomas, and others
subfiles.summary: A coalition of civic leaders urges President Truman to place the Japanese Mandated Islands under United Nations trusteeship. They strongly advocate civilian rather than military administration for these islands, Guam, and American Samoa.
subfiles.title: Telegram to President Truman Urging Civilian Trusteeship for Pacific Islands

subfiles.about: Drafts a reply acknowledging John Collier's telegram to the President concerning the Japanese Mandated Islands.
subfiles.summary: Preliminary draft reply to John Collier acknowledging his telegram concerning trusteeship and future administration of the Japanese Mandated Islands.
subfiles.title: Draft Letter to John Collier Regarding Trusteeship Administration

subfiles.about: Revises the draft reply to John Collier regarding United States leadership in the United Nations trusteeship system.
subfiles.summary: Revised draft reply from Alger Hiss to John Collier affirming American commitment to the United Nations trusteeship system.
subfiles.title: Revised Draft Letter to John Collier Concerning Trusteeship Policy

subfiles.about: Communicates the official State Department position on trusteeship and administration of dependent territories to John Collier.
subfiles.summary: Official letter from Alger Hiss to John Collier affirming United States support for United Nations trusteeship and dependent peoples.
subfiles.title: Letter to John Collier on Trusteeship for Non-Self-Governing Territories

subfiles.about: Analyzes the interdepartmental dispute over applying national treatment versus closed door policies in the Japanese Mandated Islands.
subfiles.summary: Analyzes State-Navy disagreements in SWNCC over national treatment versus most-favored-nation treatment for commerce in the Japanese Mandated Islands.
subfiles.title: Terms Trusteeship for the Japanese Mandated Islands

subfiles.about: Transmits provisional British draft terms of trusteeship for Tanganyika resulting from discussions in London.
subfiles.summary: Transmits provisional British draft terms of trusteeship for Tanganyika following discussions in London and notes comments on specific articles.
subfiles.title: Covering Letter Transmitting Draft Terms of Trusteeship for Tanganyika

subfiles.about: Outlines sixteen draft articles establishing terms of trusteeship for the British mandate of Tanganyika.
subfiles.summary: Draft agreement outlining sixteen articles under which the United Kingdom would administer Tanganyika as a United Nations trust territory. It establishes terms for defense, native rights, equal commercial treatment, education, and Trusteeship Council oversight.
subfiles.title: Draft Terms of Trusteeship for Tanganyika

subfiles.about: Urges the United States to acquire and develop former Spanish Pacific islands for defense and commercial purposes.
subfiles.summary: Spanish-language letter urging the United States to retain and develop the Marshall, Mariana, and Caroline islands for commerce and defense.
subfiles.title: Letter Concerning United States Retention of Pacific Islands

subfiles.about: Reports on a British statement to the Far Eastern Commission regarding Japanese occupation costs and transmits a proposed response.
subfiles.summary: Transmits British Embassy statement regarding Japanese occupation costs and gold reserves, together with General McCoy's prepared response.
subfiles.title: U.K. Statement on U.S. Occupation Costs Proposal

subfiles.about: Presents the British view that Japanese gold and precious metals should be reserved for reparations rather than occupation costs.
subfiles.summary: Sets forth the British position that Japanese gold and precious metals should be allocated to reparations without offsetting occupation costs.
subfiles.title: Statement by United Kingdom Delegation on Occupation Costs and Reparations

subfiles.about: Maintains that the Basic Post-Surrender Policy controls the application of reparations to occupation costs.
subfiles.summary: Affirms the United States position that the Basic Post-Surrender Policy controls the disposition of Japanese reparations relative to occupation costs.
subfiles.title: Statement by General Frank R. McCoy on Reparations and Occupation Costs

subfiles.about: Provides occupation expenditure data for Japan under GARIOA appropriations for use by the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.summary: Furnishes Japanese occupation cost figures under GARIOA appropriations for disease prevention and civilian relief to the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.title: Letter Regarding United States Occupation Costs in Japan

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of General Richards's letter transmitting Japanese occupation expenditure statistics.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate copy of the Department of the Army letter furnishing Japanese occupation expenditure statistics under the GARIOA appropriation.
subfiles.title: Duplicate Copy of Letter on Japanese Occupation Costs

subfiles.about: First-page copy of General Richards's letter regarding Japanese occupation costs under GARIOA.
subfiles.summary: First-page copy of General Richards's letter regarding Japanese occupation costs and GARIOA funding.
subfiles.title: Partial Duplicate Copy of Letter on Japanese Occupation Costs

subfiles.about: Proposes legal and administrative means for SCAP to prevent China or the Soviet Union from expanding occupation forces in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Advises how the United States and SCAP can legally and administratively prevent China or the Soviet Union from increasing occupation forces.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Preventing Chinese or Soviet Increase of Occupation Forces in Japan

subfiles.about: Transmits Vice Consul Pfeiffer's memorandum reporting on occupation conditions in Okinawa.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Vice Consul Pfeiffer's memorandum on the economic, political, and social problems facing the American occupation of Okinawa.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 109 Transmitting Report on Conditions in Okinawa

subfiles.about: Provides an extensive evaluation of economic distress, administrative difficulties, and social conditions in occupied Okinawa.
subfiles.summary: Comprehensive memorandum analyzing living conditions, economic destruction, and military administration in occupied Okinawa. Vice Consul Pfeiffer details acute housing shortages, typhoon damage, malaria buffer zones, low wages, currency conversion, and the alienation of local goodwill caused by indifferent Military Government policies. He emphasizes that the local civilian administration feels powerless and concludes that successful rehabilitation requires long-term planning, economic reconstruction, and eventual reintegration with Japan.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Conditions in Okinawa
